cohort: All live births recorded in the Brazilian Ministry of Health's Live Births Panel between 2019 and 2021, totaling 5,522,910 deliveries.
finding: Between 2019 (pre-COVID-19 pandemic) and 2021 (the first full year of the COVID-19 pandemic), there was a statistically significant increase in both prematurity and Cesarean Section Rate (CSR) in Brazil, and these increases showed a moderate positive correlation.
mod_finding: The Cesarean Section Rate (CSR) in Brazil increased from 56.34% to 57.05% (p<0.01) between 2019 and 2021, and this increase was positively correlated with the rise in prematurity during the COVID-19 pandemic.
cross-section timing: Data was analyzed for the years 2019 (pre-pandemic) and 2021 (pandemic).
